groups.name: color
groups.description: Semantic tokens: the vocabulary components (via component tokens) and apps consume. Values here are the light theme (the default). Other themes override this contract via stylex.createTheme — see ./themes.

groups.name: brand
groups.description: Brand colours for decoration and illustration: wordmarks, gradients, empty states, charts. Never for text or control boundaries; those use `color`, which is contrast-audited.

groups.name: shadow
groups.description: Elevation for floating surfaces (popovers, dialogs). Shadows are deliberately subtle and rely on a border for definition, so one value reads correctly in both light and dark themes.

groups.name: size
groups.description: Fixed dimensions. Control heights are the same on every device; the smallest (controlSm, 32px) is above WCAG 2.5.8's 24px minimum target.

groups.name: focus
groups.description: One focus ring for the whole system.

groups.name: motion
groups.description: Motion. Durations collapse to 0ms under prefers-reduced-motion here, at the token level, so every transition and entrance animation in the system respects it automatically. `spin` slows rather than stops: a loading spinner is a functional status indicator, not decoration.

groups.name: buttonTokens
groups.description: Component tokens: the third tier (primitive → semantic → component). Every colour a component paints comes from its own group here. Defaults alias semantic tokens, so they follow the active theme automatically. A theme overrides a component token directly only where the semantic alias isn't right for that component (see themes/dark.ts: the switch). This is what lets a brand restyle one component, e.g. pill-shaped secondary buttons with a tinted background, without touching the semantic layer every other component shares. Each component has two groups: `*Tokens` (colour, themed per mode) and `*Shape` (radius, border weight, type, shadow, motion: themed per brand). Splitting them is what lets a brand change a button's whole character (pill vs square, uppercase mono vs sentence case) once, while light/dark stays a colour-only concern. Aliases resolve where they're declared (:root), which is why themes are applied to <html>. A theme class on a nested element would re-skin semantic tokens but not the component aliases computed above it.

groups.name: fieldTokens
groups.description: TextField input and Select trigger: the "text-like control" surface.

groups.name: fieldsetTokens
groups.description: Fieldset: a labelled group of related fields.

groups.name: textTokens
groups.description: Heading and Text. One tone per role, so a brand can retint headings alone.

groups.name: linkTokens
groups.description: Link. Always underlined, so colour alone never marks it (WCAG 1.4.1).

groups.name: cardTokens
groups.description: Card: a surface that groups content. Its edge is decorative.

groups.name: badgeTokens
groups.description: Badge: a short status label. Each `*Fg` carries 4.5:1 on its `*Bg`.

groups.name: codeTokens
groups.description: Code blocks: source on a raised surface, with syntax colours. Every syntax colour is text and needs 4.5:1 on `bg`; colour is never the only cue, since the code reads the same without it.

groups.name: tabsTokens
groups.description: Tabs. The selected indicator carries 3:1 against the surface it sits on.

tokens.description: Hover wash for rows, menu items, ghost buttons.

Status washes (alerts, badges). Each carries its matching `fg*` status colour and `fgDefault` at 4.5:1.
Gradient text (display headings, wordmark). Both ends meet 4.5:1 on canvas and surface, so the whole gradient is readable.
Decorative dividers and surface edges (no contrast requirement).
Boundaries that identify a control: ≥3:1 against canvas and surface.
Responsive: horizontal page padding. Tighter on phones so content keeps its width; components never need their own breakpoint for this.
Dialogs and hero cards.
Display sizes, for page and hero headings.
Display type is optically loose at large sizes; tighten it.
Small caps / overline labels.
Switch thumb: lifts it off the track.
Raised cards on the canvas.
Checkbox / radio box.
Layout widths for app shells consuming the system.
Surfaces, inputs, dividers.
Small selection controls, where 1px reads as too faint.
Loading spinners keep turning under reduced motion (they're a status indicator, so stopping them would hide that work is happening), but at less than half the speed.
